title: GitHub - peterretief/codemap: One HTML page that maps a Go module: packages, dependencies, files and functions
excerpt: One HTML page that maps a Go module: packages, dependencies, files and functions - peterretief/codemap
content_html:
One HTML page that maps a Go module: every package, what it builds on within the module, and the functions in each of its files. Search it, click a package to see what it uses and what uses it, and, for a module on GitHub, jump to any function's line. Tests are left out.

Open that example to try it.

Use it

In your module's folder, with Go 1.24 or later:

go run github.com/peterretief/codemap@latest -o code-map.html

Then open code-map.html in a browser. It's one file with nothing to serve, so it can go on any website. -root DIR maps another folder.

It's been checked against a plain-text count on cobra, gin, hugo, prometheus and kubernetes: packages, files and functions all match. Kubernetes (1,278 packages, 34,823 functions) takes under 2 seconds and makes a 4.5 MB page.

In GitHub Actions

- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: peterretief/codemap@v0.2.0
  with:
    output: code-map.html
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: code-map
    path: code-map.html

How it reads the map

  • Each row builds only on the rows below it, so the foundations are at the bottom and your commands at the top.
  • A long row wraps onto more lines, and the map scrolls, so names stay readable however big the module is.
  • Wider boxes have more functions, and colours are top-level folders.
  • Lines show direct links; ones already implied by others appear when you pick a package.
  • internal/ is left off names. vendor, testdata and folders with their own go.mod are left out.
  • The page loads its fonts from Google Fonts, and falls back to system fonts without them.

Other languages

perl-codemap does the same for Perl.

Licence

MIT
